note: What the frontier Harbor path runs (internal-task plan, Implementation steps 1 and 2). materialize.ts checks every task against these digests; agents.py reads harnesses and models; vm-run.sh installs Harbor from the wheel below and refuses another hash; egress.py applies the blocklist. A change here is a reviewed pin change, made before the preregistration it serves.

harbor.licence: Apache-2.0 (wheel metadata License-Expression and github.com/harbor-framework/harbor LICENSE, checked 2026-11-07)

dependencies.how: uv 0.13.4 pip compile of harbor==0.24.0 for Python 3.12 on x86_64-manylinux_2_28 with --generate-hashes; the harbor line keeps only the pinned wheel hash. vm-run.sh installs it with uv pip install --require-hashes --only-binary :all:, so every package around the wheel is pinned by version and hash and nothing is built from source.

task_selection.rule: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks whose pooled pass rate over DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at high effort, pooled across the five harnesses at the top of that model on the board (mini-swe-agent, Kimi Code, Hermes, Pi, Claude Code; 3 attempts each, so 15 trials per task), is below the threshold. 52 of the 87 scored TB2.1 tasks qualify.

source.board: Harness Leaderboard (Joel Niklaus, Hugging Face Space joelniklaus/harness-leaderboard), board v0.1.1
source.trials: the public bucket trials-*.jsonl of the -full- runs on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash high, read 2026-11-07 by internal-task (~/.capy/work/hl/analyze.py on its machine)
source.derived_file: handoffs/internal-task/data/difficulty_ds_high.json in the Harness Evals Captain drive
source.licence: the Space is Apache-2.0 (its README); the bucket states no licence of its own, so only the derived per-task rates of the selected tasks are kept here, never the leaderboard trial files
source.attribution: Task list derived from the Harness Leaderboard by Joel Niklaus (Apache-2.0).

task_selection.tree_rule: sha256 over the 52 task ids in sorted order, one line '<task id>\0<source digest>\n' each; a source digest is treeDigest of tasks/<id>/ at the commit (scripts/gstack-laneb/pinned/quick/laneb/runner/materialize.ts: sha256 over '<relative path>\0<file sha256>\n' for every file, sorted)
task_selection.image_digests: registry-1.docker.io manifest digests of each task.toml docker_image tag, resolved 2026-11-07; materialize.ts rewrites docker_image to <repo>@<digest>

kept_selection.rule: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks whose pooled pass rate on the same board data as task_selection (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash high, five harnesses, 15 trials per task) is at or above the threshold, sorted by sha256('<seed>\0<id>') as lowercase hex, ties by id; the first 8. 35 of the 87 scored TB2.1 tasks qualify. A kept-stage cell runs these 8 at 1 attempt, reported separately from the 52 (internal-task plan, Big decisions 2).
kept_selection.image_digests: registry-1.docker.io manifest digests of each task.toml docker_image tag, resolved 2026-11-07

shared_order.rule: the 52 task ids sorted by sha256('<seed>\0<id>') as lowercase hex, ties by id (none occur); every cell uses this order, so the first n tasks of any cut are a paired uniform random subset

anthropic.why: Hermes v0.23.1 needs the anthropic SDK for its native Anthropic provider and imports it lazily (agent/anthropic_adapter.py _require_sdk); install.sh's locked [all] sync leaves it out (pyproject.toml [all] note: removed 2026-05-12, covered by lazy-install), and our config turns lazy installs off, so an install without it fails a Claude cell with "The 'anthropic' package is required for the Anthropic provider".
anthropic.install: agents.py FrontierHermes.install: install.sh and every later step run under HERMES_HOME=/tmp/hermes (amendment 5); after install.sh, hermes pm install --extra anthropic adds the pyproject anthropic extra to the environment Hermes's package manager committed, the one the hermes launcher runs on (Hermes's own uv.lock at v0.23.1 pins anthropic==0.125.0); then that environment must import anthropic 0.125.0

openrouter_plugin.name: he-openrouter-effort
openrouter_plugin.why: Hermes's built-in openrouter provider sends OpenRouter's reasoning field only when the base URL's host is openrouter.ai (run_agent.py _is_openrouter_url, agent/reasoning_params.py _supports_reasoning_extra_body) and reads config extra_body only for custom providers (agent/agent_init.py _custom_provider_extra_body_for_agent), as of v0.23.1, so behind the metering proxy it sends no effort and no output cap. This llm_request middleware (Hermes's documented plugin hook, hermes_cli/middleware.py) adds reasoning {effort: high} and max_completion_tokens (HE_OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) to every request on provider openrouter and changes nothing else. Declared configuration of amendment 1 of frontier-shootout-2026-11; frontier_settings.py refuses a file whose sha256 differs (HE-FRONTIER-015)

xai:grok-4.7.source: openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/x-ai/grok-4.7/endpoints, read 2026-11-15 (xAI's endpoint: context_length 500,000, max_completion_tokens 450,000). max_output_tokens is the 128,000 cap every other model here runs under, below that ceiling
xai:grok-4.7.api: xAI's Responses API (POST /v1/responses) on the metering proxy's xai route, effort high, for every harness that runs it, each on its own xAI route: Grok Build, Pi (its xai catalog row chat:grok-4.7, api openai-responses), Hermes (its xai provider, api_mode codex_responses) and OpenClaw (its bundled xai provider, api openai-responses). The proxy refuses previous_response_id and forces store false (HE-PROXY-013); each harness asks for the encrypted reasoning and replays it in full on every turn, relying on no stored response (tests/frontier-harbor-replay.test.ts). Hermes at the pinned commit sends no reasoning effort for grok-4.7 (its Grok effort allowlist stops at grok-4.6), so xAI's default for the model, high, applies. Chat Completions is not used: xAI documents it as deprecated for these models, returning no reasoning content and with no field for the encrypted reasoning, so every multi-turn or tool-calling conversation through it discards the model's earlier thinking and results from it understate what Grok reasoning models can do (docs.x.ai, model-capabilities/text/comparison and the API best practices, read 2026-11-16). The proxy's xai route also forwards /v1/chat/completions, which none of these configs uses

openrouter:moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro.source: openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro/endpoints, read 2026-11-15: Moonshot AI's endpoints (moonshotai/mxfp4 at $2 / $10, moonshotai/highspeed at $4 / $20) have context_length 1,048,576 and max_completion_tokens 943,718; the max_price at the $2 / $10 row keeps requests off highspeed. max_output_tokens is the 128,000 cap every other model here runs under
openrouter:moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro.api: OpenAI Chat Completions only (POST /v1/chat/completions on the metering proxy's OpenRouter route). The proxy pins every request to Moonshot AI's endpoint: it adds provider {only: [moonshotai], allow_fallbacks: false, max_price at the price row} and refuses the trial when the response names another served provider than Moonshot AI

openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.3.source: openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/z-ai/glm-5.3/endpoints, read 2026-11-16: Baidu's endpoint (provider Baidu, tag baidu/fp8, quantization fp8, service_tier null) has context_length 1,048,576 and max_completion_tokens 131,072, and lists tools, tool_choice (auto and none, not required), reasoning, include_reasoning, reasoning_effort and max_tokens among its supported_parameters. max_output_tokens is the 128,000 cap every other model here runs under
openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.3.api: OpenAI Chat Completions only (POST /v1/chat/completions on the metering proxy's OpenRouter route). Served by Baidu at fp8 (host baidu, precision fp8; provider-terms ruling, 2026-11-16). The proxy pins every request to that one endpoint: it adds provider {only: [baidu/fp8], allow_fallbacks: false, max_price at the price row} and service_tier default, refuses a request that sets another service_tier or speed, and refuses the trial when the response names another served provider than Baidu or another tier

effort.anthropic: adaptive thinking plus output_config.effort = high, set through each harness own setting
effort.openai: reasoning effort high (Responses reasoning.effort or chat reasoning_effort), set through each harness own setting
effort.particle: reasoning_effort high on Chat Completions, set through each harness own setting (docs.particle.ai/reasoning: medium and high both select Particle-1's high effort, which is also its default when no effort is sent)
effort.google: Gemini's generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel HIGH on generateContent and streamGenerateContent, set through each harness own setting (amendment 2 of frontier-shootout-2026-11; Hermes v0.23.1 writes it in lower case, high, as Google's own REST examples do); the proxy records it per request as thinking_level
effort.openrouter: OpenRouter's reasoning {effort: high} on Chat Completions, set through each harness own setting (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 offers none, low, high and max; Pi 1.5.0's catalog thinkingLevelMap); on Hermes the he-openrouter-effort plugin sets it (amendment 1 of frontier-shootout-2026-11), and no top-level reasoning_effort is sent

egress.how: Harbor 0.24.0 docker environments know three network modes (public, no-network, allowlist) and no blocklist. egress.py subclasses Harbor DockerEnvironment: its egress sidecar (a copy of Harbor harbor-docker-egress-control-sidecar, gost 3 transparent proxy plus nftables, Apache-2.0) gains a blocklist service, the sidecar runs for every trial, and the public mode (every TB2.1 phase, allow_internet = true) redirects all TCP from the task containers through gost, which sniffs the TLS SNI or the HTTP Host of each connection and refuses a host on the list. Non-TCP egress other than DNS is rejected, as in Harbor allowlist mode. A trial whose sidecar cannot start (no nftables inet) fails instead of running unblocked.

why.cursor.sh: Cursor's API hosts, with every *.cursor.sh host (https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/network-configuration): reachable from Cursor cells only (cursor_cells below), so no other cell can reach Cursor's backend
why.downloads.cursor.com: Cursor's package host (network-configuration page: client updates); a Cursor cell installs the pinned CLI package from it, no other cell needs it

cursor_cells.how: egress.py CursorBlocklistDockerEnvironment, the environment plan.ts names for a cell of harness cursor and no other: the same sidecar built from egress-sidecar/Dockerfile.cursor, which installs blocklist-cursor.txt (this blocklist) in place of blocklist.txt. gost has no exceptions to a wildcard, so this list leaves out cursor.sh, *.cursor.sh and downloads.cursor.com and names Cursor's hosts for other purposes one by one

allowed.api2.cursor.sh: the CLI's default endpoint (agent --help: -e/--endpoint, default "https://api2.cursor.sh", harnesses/cursor/cli-help.txt); the one host the CLI tried at run time with no key (harnesses/cursor/README.md: the install check's egress.ndjson, 4 denials of api2.cursor.sh:443 over 2 turns); network-configuration page: most API requests
allowed.downloads.cursor.com: the pinned package URL (harnesses/cursor/pin.json integrity.package_url); network-configuration page: client updates. Needed at install, inside the same trial; --disable-auto-update keeps the CLI from updating itself

cursor_cells.allowed_sources_note: these are harnesses/cursor/pin.json model_cursor.egress_hosts plus downloads.cursor.com. cli-config.observed.json (what the CLI wrote at run time with no key) names no host. The Harbor sidecar logs no host decision, so the hosts a keyed Harbor trial really reaches are not recorded per trial
cursor_cells.limits: A cursor.sh host the network-configuration page does not name is not refused in a Cursor cell (the multi-user CONNECT allowlist refuses it). Every other host is as for every cell

egress.limits: A blocklist by host name cannot block one path of a shared host without TLS interception, which would change every task image trust store. So github.com (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1, laude-institute/terminal-bench, laude-institute/terminal-bench-2), raw.githubusercontent.com, codeload.github.com and huggingface.co (datasets zai-org/terminal-bench-2-verified, openguardrails/terminal-bench-2.1-deepseek-v4-flash-trajectories, the leaderboard bucket) stay reachable, because tasks use those hosts for legitimate downloads. Fetches from them are caught by the audit of captured requests (plan step 5), where a confirmed answer-key receipt scores a fail. A client that hides its SNI (ECH) or connects by IP literal with no SNI and no Host header is not matched; DNS is not filtered.

broker.how: vm-run.sh runs broker.ts on 127.0.0.1: at agent setup each installed-agent class asks it for its trial slot; the broker binds slot <trial> in the metering proxy (key trial-token:<trial>, a fresh token trial-token:<trial>.<32 hex>, the cell model plus the harness housekeeping model as the slot model list) with the proxy control token it alone holds, and returns only the token and the base URL. The token is the only credential the container sees.

git_static.why: 50 of the 60 pinned task images have no git; the workspace git setup (egress.py, frontier_settings.WORKSPACE_GIT) copies this static git into a container whose image has none, the same in every arm, so the starting repository and the agent's git are there in every trial. It is a full git with https: harness installers (Hermes clones its source over https) and task solutions (train-fasttext, compile-compcert) clone over https once they find a git, so a git without https breaks them
git_static.source: github.com/baulk/git-minimal release v2.56.0, flavor git-minimal-musl: git v2.56.0 built on musl and linked statically, with libcurl (and its TLS library and CA bundle) linked in, so https remotes work in an image with no CA store
git_static.launcher: the links point at install_dir/cmd/<name>, the release's launcher (cmd/git-minimal), which finds install_dir from /proc/self/exe and sets GIT_EXEC_PATH and GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR before running bin/git, so the whole tree is copied as it unpacks (symlinks included). The release's curl launcher is not linked
git_static.shadows: an image whose own git comes later (apt-get install git during a trial) still runs this git first: /usr/local/bin comes before /usr/bin on PATH
git_static.checked: 2026-11-10, in a debian:bookworm-slim container with no other git and no CA store: git --version, git init with the release's templates (hooks/ present), the workspace git setup, a local-path and a file:// clone, fetch, a branch push, rev-parse origin/main, git ls-remote on https://github.com/git/git.git and a depth-1 https clone all worked
